m2c/tests/auth/auth_fixtures.py -- Patch C03: fixtures for the login tests.

Why this is not a conftest.py: tests/test_doctor.py does ``from conftest import
...``, which resolves by module name, and a second conftest.py in tests/auth
would shadow the real one.  So these fixtures live in an ordinary module that
each test file under tests/auth imports explicitly (``from auth_fixtures import
*``).  That also keeps the autouse fixtures below scoped to the auth tests; a
plugin or a nested conftest would apply them to every test in the suite.

The parent conftest already points M2C_HOME and HOME at a temp directory for
every test.  This module adds, for the auth tests only:

* ``_no_real_keyring`` (autouse): the OS keyring is replaced by "not
  available" so no test can read or write a developer's real keychain, even
  on a machine where the optional ``keyring`` package is installed.  Tests
  that want a keyring ask for ``fake_keyring``.
* ``_fresh_token_cache`` (autouse): the in-memory JWT cache is module state,
  so it is emptied around every test.
* ``server``: a started ``MockServer``; the test fails if the client made a
  call nobody scripted.
* ``fake_time``: a ``FakeTime``.
* ``m2c_logs``: caplog, attached directly to the ``m2c`` logger at DEBUG.
  ``cli.main`` turns propagation off on that logger, so plain caplog would
  silently see nothing; attaching to the logger itself also means the tests
  read the RAW records (no ContentFreeFilter in the way), which is stricter

m2c/tests/auth/mock_server.py -- Patch C03: a scripted stand-in for the S03
device endpoints, plus the helpers the auth tests share.

The server is a real ``http.server`` on 127.0.0.1 (random port), so the tests
drive the genuine ``urllib`` code path in m2c.auth.login: sockets, headers,
redirects, dropped connections and all.  Time is the only thing faked (see
``FakeTime``): the server answers instantly, and the client's sleeps and
deadline run on a clock the test controls, so a "10 minute" login takes
milliseconds.

Scripting.  ``server.script("pair/poll", reply1, reply2, ...)`` queues the
replies for one path; each request pops the next.  When a script runs dry the
request is recorded in ``server.unscripted`` and answered with a 500, and the
``server`` fixture fails the test -- an unexpected extra call is a bug in
either the test or the client.  ``repeat_last=True`` keeps answering with the
final reply (for "pending forever").

The secret constants below are what the mock server hands out.  Each is
distinctive so a leak is unmistakable, and each satisfies the real S03 shapes
(token_urlsafe(32)-like for the codes, three dot-separated parts for the JWT,
a UUID for the device id).

m2c/tests/auth/test_auth_redaction.py -- Patch C03: the device code, the
device credential and the JWT never appear in logs, tracebacks, exception
messages, reprs, stdout or stderr.

This is the "Done when" item that matters most, so it is attacked from
several sides:

* every outcome of a login (success and each failure) is run with the raw log
  records captured, and everything is searched for the three secrets;
* errors are *forced* in the places that hold secrets -- including a server
  that echoes the secrets back in its error bodies, and approvals whose
  secret is malformed in a way that keeps the secret text inside the bad
  value -- and the exceptions are rendered every way an error tracker or
  ``pytest --showlocals`` would (str, repr, vars, traceback, traceback WITH
  local variables);
* the real program is run in a subprocess and its stderr is searched;
* the source is scanned so a future edit cannot quietly add a logging call.

m2c/tests/auth/test_auth_token.py -- Patch C03: load_credential() for the
device link, and get_access_token() for later HTTP calls.

The token helper exchanges the stored device credential for a short-lived JWT
(POST /v1/code/devices/token -> {jwt, expires_in}), keeps it in memory and
refreshes it a safety margin before it expires.  A revoked device is a
specific, non-retryable error; transient problems are retryable ones.  Nothing
in Wave 2 or 3 calls this yet, so the tests are what pin its behaviour.
